items.title: Earl King Interview, 1980-04-10
items.q: And this is a record you played on by U. Smith.

ctx.x: You had to do it. They're looking at the clock constantly. They want to know how fast you're going to get it done and get out of it. They were walking about $12 an hour, and today they charge you $150 an hour, you know. It's a difference. And now they go in the studio nowadays and stay in there, and it's infinite, you know. But, uh, you had to get the whole ball of wax done, the rhythm, the arms, a whole lot of sound. Yeah.

Everything was done all at one time. Yeah. Everything was a big ball in there. It was tension in there, you know. You played on a lot of sets. Besides your own recording, you played on a lot of other people's recordings. And this is a record you played on by U. Smith. It's called Rockin' the Moans and Boogie Wee Blue. I wanna jump on my way out and fall.

I wanna hide what my giant school's called. Young men with a child I hold on and do. I got a rockin' the moans and a boogie boogie. On the mountain, baby, that ain't all.
